title: The Withdrawal Hold
intro: A text says a large withdrawal from your Ostrel account is "on hold".
You did not ask for any withdrawal. Your heart skips.

notify.text: Withdrawal of 0.62 BTC on hold. Not you? Call…

screen.context: You have not asked to withdraw anything from Ostrel.

msg: Call our fraud team now on

phone.label: Call this number
phone.lens: A phone number in the text is the hook.
phone.why: The scam is the call. The "fraud team" will walk you into moving your coins.

amount.label: A big scary amount
amount.lens: A huge withdrawal you never made.
amount.why: The shock is meant to make you panic.

timer.label: Released in minutes
timer.why: Pressure stops you from checking in the app.

notyou.label: "Not you? Call us"
notyou.lens: It sends you to a number instead of the app.
notyou.why: A real alert tells you to open the app.

newaddr.label: Hidden details
newaddr.lens: It names no address and no time.
newaddr.why: Real alerts show details you can check in the app.

sender.label: Ostrel Alerts
sender.why: Sender names can be faked. Check inside the app.

time.label: Sent at 3:12 AM
time.why: Scams are sent at any hour. The time proves nothing.

actions.label: Open the Ostrel app and check my withdrawals
Delete it and report the text as junk

trap.title: Ostrel Fraud Team (call)
trap.ask: The "agent" says your coins are at risk and asks you to move them to a "safe wallet" now.

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. Your phone company can now block more of these texts.

verify.line: The app showed no withdrawal at all. The text was fake. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You ignored it safely. Reporting would help protect others.

go_ahead.line: The "agent" had you move your coins to a "safe wallet". It was theirs.

what_if.go_ahead: The app would have shown no withdrawal at all. Checking there first takes ten seconds.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting the text helps others.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring it was safe. A quick report protects others.

golden_rule: If a scary alert gives you a phone number, do not call it. Open the app yourself.

quick_check.q: A text says a big withdrawal is on hold and tells you to call a number to cancel it. You never asked for one. What do you do?

options.text: Do not call. Open the app yourself and report the text

quick_check.explain: The number belongs to the scammers. Your own app shows what is real.

hints.nudge: Where does the text want you to go?

rows.v: None in the app this week
Shows the address and time in the app

rows.k: A "fraud team" that asks you to move coins
